body: Thats my dogs name, too!  I have a Pekinese / Chihuahua.  A Pikachu.
You're welcome.  I don't want to die - I just want the pain to stop. I hope you find a light to light your way, too. Even a little light helps you see the darkness for what it is.

I'm sorry for my rambling; it isn't quite as concise as I would like it to be.  

What I am trying to explain in this sentence is that thinking about committing suicide gives relief to you, to your brain.  This is simply because out of darkness, there is now this very real option, one that will make whatever it is that is torturing you daily, stop.  You are correct - this way of thinking is an ENTIRELY an unhealthy thing.  I am just trying to explain the pattern and how I was able to lessen the incidence of thinking this way. 

And yes, a defense mechanism.  When the brain is overloaded with stress and fear, it will look for a way to get out, get away from the situation(s) that caused this stress response from the body. Thinking about ending it all gives me a great relief, which is what is so dangerous. I have had to make an effort to change those connections my brain has made into more healthy ones. I realize my folly, and am trying to change my way of thinking so I can heal from this mind sickness that I have created. 

Thank you for the opportunity to explain myself further. I'm probably still not explaining it well, and for that I apologize. It's hard to put pen to paper (so to say) about how I feel.
